title: Pizza with meat (no pepperoni), school lunch, medium crust

content.title: About
content.content: A pizza topped with a mix of meats such as ham, chicken, or beef, without pepperoni, served as part of a school lunch. The medium crust (3415) provides a balanced crunch and softness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional school pizza is often produced in large batches to ensure consistent taste and quality.
Meat toppings without pepperoni usually contain less sodium than classic pepperoni.
The medium crust (size 3415) was designed for an optimal dough‑to‑topping ratio, making the pizza easy to hold.
School menus often fortify pizza with vitamins and minerals to meet children’s nutritional requirements.
The dough for a medium crust typically uses a modest amount of yeast, allowing faster baking in industrial ovens.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Meat toppings provide high‑quality protein essential for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Meat and whole‑grain dough contribute B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Moderate fiber
items.content: If whole‑grain flour is used, the crust adds dietary fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheese layer provides calcium important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cured meat slices and cheese can increase overall salt intake, which should be monitored.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Meat toppings and cheese add saturated fats, which may be a concern for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger reactions in individuals allergic to milk proteins.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional crust contains gluten, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pizza is conveniently eaten by hand, cut into bite‑size slices. Adding fresh vegetables such as tomatoes or cucumber, or a sprinkle of herbs, can boost its nutritional profile.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in an oven or microwave to keep the crust crisp.
